title: VPC upgrade staging windows, partition tolerance & operator safety (PRD)
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Problem statement: Private/VPC customers require a safe, observable, and testable upgrade path that tolerates transient network partitions and supports offline/air-gapped environments. Current acceptance criteria in existing PRDs focus on egress and mirror flows but lack a clear staging-window contract, explicit operator safety modes, and deterministic rollback triggers when upgrade cohorts encounter partial partitioning or degraded bootstrap mirrors.

Goal: Define explicit requirements and acceptance criteria for staging windows, partition-tolerance behavior, operator safety modes, and rollback conditions for Private/VPC upgrades. Provide a concrete rollout and verification plan (canary cohorts, bandwidth gating, checksum validation, and operator-runbook steps) that works both online and air-gapped.

Scope: This PRD covers coordinator/operator behavior, control-plane actions during staged upgrades, observable signals for automatic/manual rollback, and guidance for offline artifact mirror validation. It excludes low-level image signing format (handled by build-security) and host-level kernel upgrades.
background: Customers operate in highly controlled networks with strict egress rules or no egress. Upgrades have occasionally caused degraded operator interactions when nodes temporarily lose mirror connectivity or when staged canaries span multiple AZs with asymmetric routing. Past incidents show unclear rollback thresholds and manual operator steps that are error-prone under time pressure. We need deterministic gates so platform teams can automate safe rollouts and meaningfully limit blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: Staging window contract: product must define 'staging windows' with three explicit modes (quiet, traffic-probed, validation-only) and documented operator pre-conditions; control-plane enforces no more than one active staging window per customer environment unless explicitly allowed by operator override.

Partition tolerance behaviour: during transient network partition (packet loss >5% or sustained RTT increase >200ms for >60s) the upgrade coordinator must pause new stage promotions and move canary instances into 'safety-hold' state; documented timeout thresholds are configurable via profile with safe defaults.

Canary cohort isolation: canary cohort size and placement must be configurable; rolling upgrades must support a 'node affinity' option that pins canaries to single AZ or single rack to measure localized failure modes before cross-AZ promotion.

Deterministic rollback triggers: define 6 observable signals (API error rate spike, token latency p95 increase, KV cache misses, failed artifact checksum, operator manual abort, mirror sync lag) and a combined scoring rule that triggers automatic rollback when score >= 2 within a 3-minute evaluation window.

Offline/air-gapped validation: when egress is restricted, an operator-run 'offline-verify' command must validate local mirror checksums, container image signatures, and operator ACLs before permitting stage promotion; a documented failure taxonomy and remediation steps must be surfaced in the console and runbook.

Operator safety modes: implement 'operator-safety' mode with options (monitor-only, pause-on-anomaly, auto-rollback) that operators can toggle per upgrade; mode state must be surfaced in Console and via API with audit logs.

Bandwidth gating and resource-aware rollout: upgrades must support bandwidth caps per-node and per-mirror-pair to avoid saturating on-site links; acceptance requires default caps and operator-configurable values, plus telemetry showing adherence during a test rollout.

Observability and tracing: per-stage dashboards with token-level latency, stage-level error breakdown, mirror sync lag, and a single aggregated health score; timeframe granularity 10s for canary cohorts.

Runbook and operator-facing messages: Console must present contextual remediation steps for each failure mode with exact kubectl/operator CLI commands and links to the offline artifact verification tool.

End-to-end test harness: CI must include a deterministic staging simulation that injects partition events and validates automatic pause/rollback behaviour; passing the harness is required for release to private-2026.04.
Documentation: update Private Deploy Upgrade Guide and operator runbook; include example YAML for staging-window profiles and a checklist for air-gapped preflight steps.
scope_changes: Added explicit operator-safety mode after initial review with SREs (previous PRDs left operator actions implicit).
Expanded acceptance criteria to include bandwidth gating and mirror checksum validation for air-gapped environments per compliance feedback.
Removed host-level kernel upgrade handling from scope; defer to infra-build team.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Documentation + feature flag behind 'staging-windows-v1' (2 weeks). Phase 1: Implement coordinator pause/resume + operator safety toggles (4 weeks) in internal test harness. Phase 2: Canaries in internal dogfood customer, low-risk cohort (10% of customers with Dedicated plan) and run deterministic partition simulation. Phase 3: Ramp to 50% with bandwidth gating enforced. Phase 4: GA for Dedicated and Private after 2 successful rolling upgrades and passing CI staging-sim tests. Each phase requires sign-off from PM, SRE lead, and Security. Air-gapped customers require offline-verify tool completion before promotion.
